proof:
# Convex base hinge erosion excludes every purely atomic bad buffered minimum

This is an actual deformation theorem, not a proof of OC. Unlike a common
homothety of a closed minor, the erosion rates below vary convexly with
the base. This preserves incoming anchored inclusions even when the
selected cap contains interior integer bases. It removes the simplex-face
and affine-center-selection premises in the earlier purely atomic branch.

## 1. Setting and statement

Let P be finite and complete in its inherited affine lattice, with k
occupied parities. Let K_z be positive d-dimensional compatible convex
fibers, d>=1, and M=sum_z V_z. Let ell be a positive affine base function
with sum_z(V_z/M)log ell(z)=0. Fix epsilon>0 and use the established
invariant buffered depth with f=(ell E/M)^(1/(d+1)) and the within-fiber
covariance norm. Its raw maximum is Q>0. Let I be the nonempty set of
integer bases carrying a maximizing mark, and k(I) its occupied parity
count. Suppose EVERY maximizing base is pure-base-bound:

    b_base(p)=Q for every p in I.                         (1)

If

    beta=Q/M < 1/k(I),                                   (2)

then this family and multiplier do not form a local minimum of the
unpenalized normalized buffered maximum. There is a positive compatible
family arbitrarily close in Hausdorff distance, with its multiplier
continuously renormalized, whose normalized buffered maximum is strictly
smaller. In particular this excludes an all-atomic joint bad minimum
with beta<Gamma_d/k, since k(I)<=k and Gamma_d<1.

This result does not exclude a mixture of atomic maximizing bases and
maximizing bases with a strict continuous cap gap. It does not silently
discard the penalty if a penalized objective is used instead.

## 2. Convex deepest regions give midpoint closure of I

The real buffered superlevel region at raw level Q is convex: every
nonvertical constraint is

    a.z+u.X-epsilon f(z,X) Gamma(u)<=c_Q(a,u),

with f jointly concave, and pure-base constraints are halfspaces. The
canonical fiber hull is also convex. Thus if p,q in I have the same
parity, choose actual maximizing marks over them. Their midpoint lies
in the convex superlevel region and its integer base lies in P. Actual
fiber compatibility puts the midpoint in that fiber. Global maximality
then implies

    (p+q)/2 in I.                                         (3)

Indeed the same argument shows I=P intersect conv(I), though only (3)
is needed below. No selected midpoint leaves the actual mixed set.

## 3. At most k(I) atomic minimizing caps cover every deepest base

For each p in I choose an attained closed base halfspace of mass Q
containing p, as supplied by (1). The family is finite. Write these
halfspaces as H_j={a_j(z)>=b_j}. Since Q<M under (2), none has the
whole P trace. Choose U_j>max(b_j,max_P a_j).

In the compact threshold box b_j<=c_j<=U_j impose that every p in I
satisfies a_j(p)>=c_j for at least one j. This is a closed condition
(a finite intersection of finite unions of closed sets) and is initially
feasible. Maximize sum_j c_j. Each nonsaturated row i, c_i<U_i,
has a witness p_i in I with

    a_i(p_i)=c_i,      a_j(p_i)<c_j for every j!=i.         (4)

Otherwise finiteness allows c_i to increase while preserving the cover.
Saturated rows select no point of P and are discarded. The remaining
closed caps G_i={a_i>=c_i}, i=1,...,m, still cover I.

Two witnesses cannot have the same parity: their midpoint is in I
by (3), and satisfies every inequality strictly by (4), contradicting
the cover. Consequently

    1<=m<=k(I).                                          (5)

Each G_i is contained in its original mass-Q cap, and contains p_i.
Its base mass is therefore at most Q, and at least b_base(p_i)=Q.
Hence EVERY one of these compressed caps has exactly mass Q:

    sum_(z in P intersect G_i) V_z=Q.                    (6)

All halfspaces here are closed. Their boundary fibers are included.

## 4. Convex hinge erosion is an actual compatible deformation

Let s_z be the surface area of K_z; for d=1 it is H_0(boundary K_z)=2.
It is finite and strictly positive. For each G_i choose a sufficiently
small number a_i^*>0 that

    h_i(z)=(a_i(z)-c_i+a_i^*)_+

is positive at every z in P intersect G_i and zero at every other
sampled base. Such a number exists because P is finite: take less than
the smallest strictly positive gap c_i-a_i(z) outside G_i. That outside
set is nonempty since Q<M. The function h_i is finite, nonnegative and
convex in the real base variables. Put

    D_i=sum_z s_z h_i(z)>0,
    h(z)=sum_(i=1)^m h_i(z)/D_i.                         (7)

For sufficiently small t>=0 define the actual fibers

    K_z(t)=K_z eroded by t h(z) times the Euclidean unit ball,
          ={X:X+t h(z) Ball subset K_z}.                 (8)

They remain positive because there are finitely many old positive
inradii. They converge to the old fibers in Hausdorff distance.

Here is the exact compatibility proof. In an anchored relation
z0=sum_j lambda_j z_j, take X_j in K_zj(t). For any unit continuous
normal u,

    u.sum_j lambda_j X_j
       <=sum_j lambda_j h_(K_zj)(u)-t sum_j lambda_j h(z_j)
       <=h_(K_z0)(u)-t h(z0).

The second inequality uses the OLD Minkowski inclusion and convexity
of the scalar rate h. These inequalities for every u say that the
convex combination belongs to K_z0(t). Thus (8) preserves all anchored
inclusions, including those with inputs outside a selected atomic cap.
The finite convex hull of the new marked fibers has exactly these
sampled fibers. No independent shrinkage of a closed minor is presumed.

The right derivative of volume under inner parallel erosion is

    V_z(t)=V_z-t s_z h(z)+o(t).                           (9)

It is also a direct special case of the already proved bounded radial
normal-roof first variation with constant inward normal speed h(z).
That proof applies to arbitrary positive convex fibers, including facets;
no smoothness assumption is introduced here. The finite number of fibers
makes all subsequent sums of the remainders o(t).

## 5. The exact mass-loss budget

Equations (7)--(9) give total first loss

    D=sum_z s_z h(z)=m.                                  (10)

For a fixed compressed cap G_i let its own captured first loss be

    D_Gi=sum_(z in G_i intersect P) s_z h(z).

Every rate is nonnegative, and the entire support of h_i on P lies in
G_i. Therefore

    D_Gi >=sum_z s_z h_i(z)/D_i=1.                        (11)

Combining (6), (9)--(11) yields, for every i,

    M_Gi(t)/M(t)
      =beta+t[beta m-D_Gi]/M+o(t)
      <=beta-t[1-beta m]/M+o(t).                         (12)

The coefficient is strictly negative by (2) and (5). This pays every
atomic covering row simultaneously using ONE actual compatible family.
There is no requirement that different cap supports be disjoint.

## 6. Covering the actual moving maximum

Every old deepest base p lies in some G_i. For EVERY point of its new
fiber, that same closed pure-base halfspace gives buffered depth at
most M_Gi(t). This bound is independent of the changing energy, source,
covariance or affine multiplier.

Renormalize ell only by the continuous positive scalar

    ell_t(z)=ell(z) exp[-sum_z V_z(t)log ell(z)/M(t)].     (13)

It is affine, positive, has the updated geometric mean one and tends
to ell. The within-fiber covariance and energy are recomputed. The
established all-direction positive-fiber buffered continuity theorem
therefore applies to this actual path. Every base outside I has a
strict old maximum gap; there are finitely many such bases. For small
t they remain below all the cap masses in (12), which tend to Q.
If I=P there are no such bases and this step is vacuous.

Thus the actual global maximum satisfies

    Q(t)/M(t) <=max_i M_Gi(t)/M(t)<beta

for all sufficiently small positive t, proving the theorem. No halfspace
orientation is omitted: arbitrary oblique competitors only decrease the
depth, whereas the fixed pure-base caps supply the needed upper covers.

## 7. Difference from the failed common contraction

For three identical interval fibers at -1,0,1, contracting the closed
minor {0,1} by a common factor violates its incoming midpoint constraint.
The hinge h(z)=(z+a)_+, 0<a<1, instead erodes the middle at rate a and
the right endpoint at rate 1+a, leaving the left endpoint unchanged.
The midpoint support inequality remains valid because 2a<=1+a. The
variable convex rates are precisely what repairs that obstruction.

The theorem resolves the purely atomic branch of an unpenalized buffered
bad minimum. A mixed menu of proper continuous and atomic maximizing
groups still needs a simultaneous covering response, and the full sharp
Gamma_d/k numerical bound remains unproved.
